headline: A Republican wants Trump Jr. subpoenaed
summary: Sen. John Curtis, a Utah Republican, asked the Senate Judiciary Committee to subpoena Donald Trump Jr. and Hunter Biden. ProPublica reported that Russian oligarch Umar Kremlev helped pay for Trump Jr.'s wedding party in the Bahamas. Curtis calls it corruption. Two Republican senators and the committee's top Democrat backed him Tuesday.

cover_question.q: Why is his dad's party after him?

cover_answer: One senator. He says the rule is the same for both parties.
table_question: When does a big gift stop being a gift?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: A senator named John Curtis wants to ask the president's son a question in front of everyone: who paid for your wedding party? A rich man from Russia paid for a lot of it. That is like a grown-up you don't know paying for your whole birthday party: your parents would want to know why. Nobody is in trouble. Asking is the senator's job.
5-7.why: A party paid for by a stranger is a picture a six-year-old already has, and the senator is the grown-up asking why.
5-7.why_long: A five-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script puts a party and a very large present in front of them and leaves the subpoena out. A grown-up asking who paid is a scene they know from their own kitchen. Expect "did he do something bad?" Nobody knows. That is why the senator wants to ask.

8-12.script: Sen. John Curtis, a Utah Republican, wants Donald Trump Jr. and Hunter Biden subpoenaed to testify. A Russian oligarch paid for much of Trump Jr.'s wedding party. Republicans investigated Biden's son, so Curtis says they must do Trump's. A referee who calls fouls on one team is no referee.
8-12.why: A chain, and a referee who calls it both ways.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out rules and whether adults apply them evenly. This story is that test in one letter: Republicans subpoenaed Hunter Biden, so Curtis says they must subpoena Trump Jr. The referee who calls fouls both ways is the mechanism. Expect "will they do it?" The committee has it and calls a hearing this year unlikely.

13-17.script: If a friend pays for your wedding, when does a gift become a payment? Sen. John Curtis, a Republican, wants Donald Trump Jr. subpoenaed after a Russian oligarch paid for much of his wedding party. Second: Curtis wants Hunter Biden subpoenaed too. Fair, or cover?
13-17.why: A gift can be a gift, and a president's son is never only a friend.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things : a wedding gift from a friend is normal, and a president's son is never only somebody's friend. Then the Hunter Biden pairing, where the argument is live: even-handed, or a way past a Republican committee. Expect "will Trump Jr. testify?" Not yet. The committee calls a hearing this year unlikely.

5-7.q: Can a friend pay for your party?
5-7.a: Yes. But when your dad is the president, people want to know who paid and what they might want back.

8-12.q: Why is his dad's party after him?
8-12.a: One senator is. He says the rule must be the same for both parties.
An order to show up and answer questions.

13-17.q: Is a wedding gift from a friend illegal?
13-17.a: The president says it was allowed and his son will repay it.

13-17.q: Why drag Hunter Biden back in?
13-17.a: Curtis says both sons deserve the same oversight. Trump Jr. has never testified under oath.
